citations.quote: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) issues this circular to inform licensed corporations that it will exempt non-centrally cleared single-stock options, equity basket options and equity index options (collectively, “non-centrally cleared equity options”) from its margin requirements1 from 4 January 2026 until further notice to align with the latest global developments.
Paragraph 7(e) of Part III of Schedule 10 to the Code of Conduct will be amended accordingly and gazetted in due course.
1 As set out in Part III of Schedule 10 to the Code of Conduct for Persons Licensed by or Registered with the Securities and Futures Commission (Code of Conduct).

reading.distinction: The factual condition for the Hong Kong exemption combines actor status (licensed corporation), product classification (single-stock, equity basket or equity index option), clearing status (non-centrally cleared), and time (from 2026-01-04 until further notice). EU and UK exemptions explain alignment but are not predicates in this model.

citations.quote: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) issues this circular to inform licensed corporations that it will exempt non-centrally cleared single-stock options, equity basket options and equity index options (collectively, “non-centrally cleared equity options”) from its margin requirements1 from 4 January 2026 until further notice to align with the latest global developments.
Paragraph 7(e) of Part III of Schedule 10 to the Code of Conduct will be amended accordingly and gazetted in due course.
1 As set out in Part III of Schedule 10 to the Code of Conduct for Persons Licensed by or Registered with the Securities and Futures Commission (Code of Conduct).

In the EU, a permanent exemption from the requirement to exchange margin for single-stock equity options and equity index options became effective on 24 December 2024, subject to monitoring and periodic reporting2.
It implemented an indefinite exemption from the UK bilateral margining requirements for single-stock equity options and index options.

reading.distinction: Product category, clearing status, regulated actor, requirement provenance and temporal continuation are separate predicates. An equity basket option is expressly included in the SFC announcement even though the overseas summaries omit that category. The SFC exemption is subject to further notice; neither the EU's permanent duration nor its monitoring and reporting conditions determine SFC eligibility. Pending gazettal is a separate legislative event, not an expressed commencement condition.

citations.quote: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) issues this circular to inform licensed corporations that it will exempt non-centrally cleared single-stock options, equity basket options and equity index options (collectively, “non-centrally cleared equity options”) from its margin requirements1 from 4 January 2026 until further notice to align with the latest global developments.
The margin requirements for non-centrally cleared equity options were originally scheduled to take effect on that date.

However, to prevent regulatory arbitrage and considering that licensed corporations’ exposures to non-centrally cleared equity options are currently insignificant, the SFC has decided to align the exemptions of its margin requirements with the approaches in the European Union (EU) and the UK:
Paragraph 7(e) of Part III of Schedule 10 to the Code of Conduct will be amended accordingly and gazetted in due course.
1 As set out in Part III of Schedule 10 to the Code of Conduct for Persons Licensed by or Registered with the Securities and Futures Commission (Code of Conduct).

reading.distinction: The first prior model conflates transaction execution and assessment time, potentially excluding a pre-2026 contract assessed after commencement. This proposal adopts the second prior model's assessment-date approach, supported by the statement that margin requirements were scheduled to take effect on that date. It also separates the industry-exposure rationale from individual eligibility: the source supplies no individual exposure threshold. Review of both prior models reveals no supported additional counterparty condition or portfolio-wide quantifier.

questions.question: No prior models were supplied for comparison. The component review supports one model; the source does not support a rival that makes gazettal a commencement prerequisite.
The full Schedule 10 provisions and three listed missing dependencies are unavailable. This model does not decide whether an underlying margin obligation would otherwise arise.
The packet does not establish the absence of subsequent notices on any assessment date. The continuation fact must not default to false.
Portfolio aggregation, mixed contracts, grandfathering and intraday commencement are not specified; no rules for those cases are inferred.

This is a consequential rival to the first prior model's execution-date interpretation, but substantively corroborates the second prior model. No additional independent rival is supported by the supplied text.
The unavailable dependencies and full Schedule 10 prevent establishing legal completeness, underlying margin obligations, counterparty conditions or transitional rules.
No portfolio aggregation rule, embedded-option allocation rule or additional actor-specific condition is supplied; none is inferred.
Absence of subsequent notice is not established by this packet and must not be assumed.
